records.meaning: Stable logical identity used to refer to a StorageObject independently of provider/path.
Catalogue object carrying identity, descriptive metadata/EAs and one or more replica locations.
Provider locator plus availability, verification, safety/lifecycle and optional node-locality evidence.
Binding/projection from a logical path to an object or view semantics.
Directory-like projection whose children are current catalogue matches for a filter.
Dynamic logical-path indirection resolved at access time with its own route policy.
Ordered TVFS-inspired composition of namespace roots with priority shadowing.
First-class extended attribute with namespace/name/type/value/provenance/authority.
Explicit tracked namespace/object changes used by TEST/DEV overlays and promotion evidence.
Pinned namespace generation used to detect stale promotion/rebase assumptions.
Real accounting domain against which free bytes, reservations and safety floors are charged.
Provider/workspace/durable role bound to a capacity domain, node and service lifecycle.
Pre-execution claim on bytes in one capacity domain.
Storage whose service/account lifecycle means it cannot count as a safe durable replica.
Safety/lifecycle evidence describing whether a provider/account is stable, temporary, credit-limited, expiring or terminating.
Measured throughput/latency evidence kept separate from provider identity and availability.
Make required bytes available in a selected workspace without changing stable object identity.
Per-candidate storage feasibility/locality/movement facts consumed by Job-to-Node Allocation.
Placement evidence classification where required inputs are already local and moving the job is the storage-cheap direction.
Placement evidence classification where required input bytes must be materialised to the candidate node.
Three distinct transfer milestones: bytes copied, integrity established, and durable provider/catalogue admission completed.
In v0.1-dev5, an AVAILABLE + VERIFIED + SAFE + STABLE location eligible to satisfy replica safety.
Availability state such as connected/available versus offline; independent from throughput and durability.
Reserved capacity intended for execution/scratch/materialisation and not necessarily safe as a sole durable store.

provenance.claim: Glossary names correspond to current executable Storage Fabric concepts/classes and planner/safety semantics.
